jobs.title: Data Center Operations Manager (Site, Facility Operations)
jobs.description:
Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own critical facility operations for one Crux site or campus — the electrical, mechanical, fire/life-safety, and controls infrastructure that keeps high-density, liquid-cooled TPU clusters continuously available. You will lead the 24/7 site facility team — chief engineer, shift technicians, and O&M contractors — and run the maintenance, procedures, drills, and change control that produce uptime, whether the building is Crux-owned or operated by a colocation partner you hold to SLA. In the early phase you will help bring the site to life: commissioning participation, acceptance, and the transition from construction to disciplined steady-state operations.



In this role, you will:

 - Establish and direct the site facility operations team — chief engineer, critical facility technicians, and contractors — with a 24/7 coverage model you design, staff, and train, maintaining highly available operations for all critical and non-critical infrastructure.

 - Operate and maintain the site’s electrical systems (utility interface through switchgear, generators, UPS, and distribution), mechanical plant (chilled water, direct-to-chip liquid cooling loops, CDUs, heat rejection), fire/life-safety, and BMS/EPMS controls.

 - Run the site maintenance program in CMMS — preventive, predictive, and corrective — with vendor and OEM service contracts managed to scope, and zero tolerance for overdue critical PMs.

 - Enforce operating discipline: SOPs/MOPs/EOPs current and rehearsed, change management on every energized system, drill program run on schedule, and monthly self-assessments presented to fleet leadership.

 - Lead site incident response for facility events end to end — detection, stabilization, escalation, root cause, corrective action — including communication when customer workloads are at risk.

 - On partner sites, manage the colocation operator to contracted SLAs: audit their maintenance records, witness their critical work, and enforce remedies when performance slips.

 - Support site bring-up: participate in commissioning through Level 5/IST, define and enforce ops acceptance criteria, tune the cooling plant to design intent in the first year, and manage warranty claims.

 - Own the site facility budget, utility coordination, and efficiency performance (PUE, WUE, energy cost), and run a safety-first culture (LOTO, energized work controls, working at height) with zero-compromise standards.



SIGNALS OF SUCCESS

After 60 days in this role:

 - Site staffing plan and 24/7 coverage model will be approved with hiring in motion.

 - Ops acceptance criteria will be agreed upon with construction/commissioning.

After 6 months:

 - CMMS is loaded with the site asset registry and PM schedules.

 - Procedures library is drafted for every critical system (or partner program audited, on a colo site).

After 1 year:

 - First site is operating with 24/7 coverage under the full standards library.

 - Preventive maintenance program is live in CMMS with zero overdue critical PMs.

 - Incident and change management program running.

 - Colo partner SLA and audit program in force at partner sites.

EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH

Experiences

 - 10+ years in critical facility or data center operations — including power generation, HVAC, or mission-critical military/industrial environments — with 5+ years managing technical teams and vendors operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure in a 24/7 environment.

 - Comprehensive working knowledge of electrical topologies (N+1/2N, UPS, generators, switchgear), mechanical and liquid cooling systems, fire/life-safety, and building automation — plus the safety programs (LOTO, hazardous energy control) that govern work on them.

 - Site bring-up or major expansion experience: commissioning participation, acceptance testing, and the construction-to-operations handoff on a mission-critical facility.

Attributes

 - Owner of the building. When the plant alarms at 2am it is yours until the site is stable and the root cause is written down. You are comfortable being the most senior Crux person on site and making the call under pressure.

 - Discipline without bureaucracy. You run tight MOPs, drills, and change control because they prevent outages, and you kill process that does not — and you can tell the difference.

Mindset

 - High tolerance for ambiguity. The site will energize before every procedure exists. You write the SOP, run it, fix it, and hand it to the next site rather than waiting for a standard to arrive.

 - AI-agentic first. Fluent with AI agents — or committed to becoming so quickly — and you embed them as first principles in how you and your team work, defaulting to agentic workflows before adding headcount or process.

Nice to have (preferred, not required)

 - 7+ years in Tier III/IV or hyperscale data center environments (Meta, Google, AWS, Microsoft, or a major colo operator).

 - Direct-to-chip liquid cooling plant operations experience (CDUs, water chemistry, loop commissioning and tuning).

 - Trade certifications (Electrical, HVAC, Controls), stationary engineer license, or military/nuclear power background.

 - CMMS/EAM administration experience and comfort with energy and reliability analytics.

 - Experience managing a colocation operator to SLA from the tenant side.

 - Full suite of other optional benefits

jobs.description:

That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own the technical and commercial vetting that turns a raw deal into a fundable project — the work that separates a defensible capacity commitment from an inflated one. When a partner asks Crux to guarantee an eight- or nine-figure sum, you're the one who tests that number against schedule, equipment composition, and real construction cost before it goes to leadership. Reporting into the Chief Program Manager's organization, you will sit at the interface between Data Center Construction, Energy, MEP, and Finance, making sure every project in the active portfolio is executed against the numbers it was approved on — and flagging it immediately when it isn't.



In this role, you will:

 - Vet the technical and commercial terms of new capacity deals — schedule, equipment cost, equipment composition — before they're recommended to leadership, right-sizing commitments rather than defaulting to the number a partner asks for.

 - Track every live data center project in the portfolio against its approved cost and schedule baseline, and own the process for flagging and escalating variance early.

 - Partner with Data Center Construction, Energy, and MEP Systems teams to translate field-level execution status into Finance-ready program reporting.

 - Own the interface between build-side execution and the cost and margin model of record — your data is what Finance's models are actually built on.

 - Run the change-control process for scope, schedule, or cost changes on active projects, with sign-off gates that keep Finance and Development aligned in real time.

 - Build and maintain the tools that make deal vetting fast and repeatable — this cannot be a one-off analysis redone from scratch on every deal.

 - Default to AI-agentic workflows for cost/schedule reconciliation and variance tracking, rather than adding headcount to keep up with portfolio growth.



SIGNALS OF SUCCESS

After 60 days in this role:

 - Deal-vetting framework (schedule, equipment cost, composition) is documented and applied to at least one live negotiation.

 - Portfolio cost/schedule tracking is live for the current active project set.

After 6 months:

 - Variance escalation process is running with a documented track record of catching at-risk projects before they slip.

 - Finance's cost and margin model of record is being fed directly from your tracking, not reconstructed separately.

After 1 year:

 - Deal-vetting and portfolio-tracking functions run as a repeatable system others can execute against, not a one-person effort.



EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH

Experiences

 - 8+ years in data center construction, capital projects, or infrastructure delivery with direct P&L, cost, or schedule ownership.

 - Demonstrated experience vetting or negotiating capacity/commercial terms against real technical and cost data, not top-down assumptions.

 - Comfortable moving fluently across finance, construction, and technology — this is not a single-lane specialist seat.

Attributes

 - “$900M is the ask” is a hypothesis until the equipment and schedule say otherwise — you test the number before you defend it.

 - You bring bad news first, unprompted, and own the result — hierarchy doesn't intimidate you and you don't intimidate easily either.

Mindset

 - High tolerance for ambiguity. The portfolio will outgrow whatever process exists today, and you build the next version rather than waiting for one.

 - AI-agentic first. Fluent with AI agents — or committed to becoming so quickly — and you embed them as first principles in how you and your team work, defaulting to agentic workflows before adding headcount or process.



Nice to have (preferred, not required)

 - Background in data center construction, controllership, or capital-projects finance specialized in the build environment.

 - Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, Level 5/IST commissioning, or other GW-scale data center technical scope.

 - Neocloud or hyperscaler experience (CoreWeave, Nebius, Nscale, Lambda, Google, AWS, Meta, Microsoft) in a program or delivery management capacity.

 - Formal cost engineering, quantity surveying, or construction finance credential.

jobs.title: Hardware Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will own everything inside the rack, physically, across Crux’s entire fleet — the TPU hosts, network switches, optics, cabling, and liquid-cooling manifolds that arrive on a truck and have to become a validated, customer-ready cluster on the date Sales committed. The role runs the full hardware lifecycle: inbound logistics and receiving, rack integration and structured cabling, power-on and validation handoff, break/fix and RMA, spares and asset records, and decommission at generation transitions — at Crux-owned campuses and at colocation sites where you hold a partner’s remote-hands team to our standard. You will build this function from zero: the deployment playbook, the spares program, the DCIM discipline, and the site technician teams that inherit them. Where Facility Operations owns the power and cooling that reach the rack, and the SRE & Software Engineering team owns the provisioning, health, and remediation software, you own the hands, the parts, and the records — a node the software has quarantined is a ticket in your queue until a technician has swapped the part and it has passed validation again. You will work hand-in-glove with Google’s hardware and support organizations, Capacity Delivery, Construction, Network Engineering, Facility Operations, the SRE & Software Engineering team, and Strategic Supply.



In this role, you will:

 - Build and lead the fleet hardware operations organization — site hardware leads, deployment technicians, and break/fix technicians — with staffing templates, shift and on-call coverage models, and training and certification standards that scale ahead of the capacity ramp; hire people better than you at their craft.

 - Own cluster deployment end to end: inbound logistics and receiving inspection, staging and secure storage, rack integration and elevations, structured fiber and copper cabling to a published standard, liquid-cooled rack installation and manifold connection with Facility Operations, power-on, and validation handoff to the SRE team — treating each cluster as a gated schedule from dock to first customer workload.

 - Run break/fix and RMA for the fleet: repair queue and SLAs by severity, parts swaps and node re-validation, RMA processing with Google and OEM/ODM partners, and failure-rate trending by component and generation that feeds back into Supply and Google.

 - Own the spares program and asset lifecycle: spares depot sizing per site against failure rates and lead times, inventory accuracy, serialized asset tracking from receipt through decommission in DCIM (NetBox or equivalent), and reconciliation to Finance’s fixed-asset register.

 - Own decommission and generation transitions: rack decommission procedures, data-bearing device sanitization and destruction with chain-of-custody, asset disposition (ITAD, return, or redeploy), and the physical sequencing of TPU generation swaps inside live facilities.

 - Manage colocation and partner remote-hands teams to Crux’s hardware standard — scopes of work, SLAs, access and escort procedures, and an audit program with witnessed work — and enforce remedies when performance slips.

 - Author and enforce the hardware operations standards library — deployment playbook, cabling and labeling standards, MOPs for energized-rack work, ESD and lifting safety, change control on production hardware — applied consistently across owned and partner sites.

 - Report fleet hardware performance to the executive team monthly — deployment velocity (racks per week versus plan), time-to-repair, spares fill rate, RMA aging, and inventory accuracy — and drive the corrective actions those numbers demand.



SIGNALS OF SUCCESS

 - 60 days — Fluent in the TPU rack, cabling, and liquid-cooling requirements set from Google; deployment playbook v1 and cabling/labeling standard drafted; DCIM platform and asset-tracking model selected with Business Systems; staffing plan and coverage model for the first site approved with hiring in motion.

 - 6 months — First cluster deployed dock-to-validation under your playbook, with racks-per-week tracked against plan; break/fix queue, RMA process with Google, and spares depot live at the first site; every serialized asset in DCIM and reconciled to Finance; partner remote-hands scope and SLA in force at any colo site.

 - 1+ year — Fleet hardware operations running as a repeatable function across multiple sites with published time-to-repair, spares fill rate, and inventory accuracy at or better than target; component failure trending informing Supply negotiations and Google escalations; first TPU generation transition executed with decommission, sanitization, and disposition clean; site hardware leads in place and owning their sites.



EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH

Experiences

 - 10+ years in data center hardware or server operations — deployment, break/fix, and asset lifecycle for large server and network fleets — including 5+ years leading technician teams across shifts and sites in a 24/7 environment.

 - Direct experience deploying high-density AI/HPC clusters: accelerator-dense racks, high-radix fabric cabling (InfiniBand, RoCE, or equivalent optical fabrics), and liquid-cooled rack installation — you have run the dock-to-validation sequence yourself, not just approved the plan.

 - Built or scaled a hardware operations program through rapid growth: deployment playbooks, spares and RMA programs, DCIM/CMDB discipline with audited inventory accuracy, and vendor or colo remote-hands management under contractual SLAs.

Attributes

 - Outcome driven and hands-on. This is a builder’s seat, not a supervisory one. You will be on the dock for the first delivery, in the cold aisle for the first rack, and on the phone with Google for the first RMA — not because there is no team, but because the person accountable for the fleet’s hardware has to be close enough to the work to change it. Then you hire people better than you at their craft and stay close enough to know when something is off before it shows up in a report.

 - Records are part of the work. You believe a swap that is not in DCIM did not happen, that inventory accuracy is a safety and financial control rather than paperwork, and that the spares depot is sized from failure data, not from a guess.

Mindset

 - Posses a high tolerance for ambiguity. Hardware will arrive before the standard is finished and the customer date will not move. You write the procedure, run it, fix it, and hand it to the next site rather than waiting for one to arrive.

 - Demonstrate velocity through discipline, not heroics. Racks per week is produced by staging, kitting, labeled cabling, and rehearsed sequences — and a deployment saved by a weekend of overtime is a playbook that failed. You build the system that makes the next cluster boring.

 - AI-agentic first. Fluent with AI agents — or committed to becoming so quickly — and you embed them as first principles in how you and your team work, defaulting to agentic workflows before adding headcount or process.



Nice to have [Preferred, not required]:

 - Hardware or server operations leadership at a hyperscaler (Google, AWS, Meta, Microsoft) or neocloud (CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Nscale or similar) during a multi-site deployment ramp.

 - Direct TPU deployment experience, or large GPU cluster deployments (NVL-class or DGX/HGX-class racks) including burn-in and validation handoff.

 - DCIM/CMDB administration (NetBox or similar), ITIL/ITSM process design, and comfort with failure-rate and inventory analytics.

 - Experience with data-bearing device sanitization standards (NIST 800-88), ITAD vendor management, and export-control handling for accelerator hardware.

 - Experience managing colocation remote-hands and smart-hands providers to SLA from the tenant side, including audit program design.

 - Safety program experience for hardware work — ESD, lifting and material handling, energized-rack MOPs, working at height.

 - Company-paid life insurance and disability

jobs.title: Head of People Operations and Systems
jobs.description:
Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure

 

Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system.

 

Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You own the technology, data, and process backbone of the People function as the company scales from startup to enterprise. 

In this role, you will:

 - Architect and build the core HR stack — HRIS as the system of record, ATS and recruiting operations, and the platforms supporting compensation cycles, benefits enrollment, and equity administration — building integrations and workflows that hold up under rapid headcount growth. 

 - Beyond systems, you serve as the operational engine behind annual comp planning, open enrollment, and multi-jurisdiction compliance, while delivering the people analytics that leadership uses to make headcount, pay, and workforce decisions.

 - Contribute broadly and have HRBP and Generalist responsibilities. 

 - Partner across Recruiting, Total Rewards, Finance, IT, and Legal.



SIGNALS OF SUCCESS

After 60 days in this role:

 - Completed a full assessment and gaps analysis of our current state. 

 - Prioritized the key projects based on OKRs and People Team priorities.

 - Ensured our ATS, Ashby, is fully integrated into the candidate and hiring manager workflows of recruiting.

 - Fully leveraged our HRIS, deel, to run core people team processes, as well as make and implement changes based on our needs and feedback.

 - Revamped our employee onboarding process and experience.

 - Adapted to a fast-paced environment, triaging appropriately and continuously improving our function.

After 6 months:

 - Demonstrated an AI-forward and automated approach to this role. You built, in a hands-on way, our core processes, models and People Team AI agents.

 - Developed our philosophy and program manage our performance & development process and prioritize key elements of our employee experience.

 - Reviewed our current benefits offering, benchmark those programs and select new offering based on our employees and competitive landscape.

 - Refined our compensation and total reward philosophy and corresponding program and administration.

After 1 year:

 - Ensure we are compliant and audit ready. 

 - Contribute to any operational workstreams in partnership with finance and legal.

 - Demonstrated consistent operational excellence and having impeccable attention to detail.

 - Implemented innovative approaches to the People Ops processes, programs and team.



EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH

Experiences

 - 8+ years experience in HR and Talent operations and systems at a leading, talent-dense, operationally rigorous company.

 - Implemented a modern HR tech stack and operated in a lean, AI-enabled environment.

 - Hands-on experience leading high visibility projects and programs in compensation, benefits, performance, L&D, recruiting and employee engagement.

Attributes

 - You are outcome driven and hands on. Close enough to the work to be useful. This is a builder's seat, not a supervisory one.

Mindset

 - You have a high tolerance for ambiguity. You absorb ambiguity and navigate complexity rather than passing it along.

Nice to have (preferred, not required)

 - Hardware, infrastructure or data center industry experience.

 - Experience in both start up and scaled enterprises.

 - HRBP,  HR Generalist, or Employee Relations experience.

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been estimated based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

About Crux

 - We offer generous base, bonus and additional incentive based compensation

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents

 - Company-paid life insurance and disability

 - Full suite of other optional benefits

 - 401(k) Plan with 4% company match

 - Hybrid schedule offering four days in-office collaboration paired with one remote workday for focused, individual work
